name: shadcn/ui
description: Customizable React components and blocks whose source becomes part of your project.

guidance.bestFor: Customizable forms, dashboards and app controls whose component code you can edit.
guidance.caveat: You own the copied code and its updates; follow the installation guide for your framework.

name: Radix UI
description: React primitives and themed components for dialogs, menus, controls and accessible interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Custom-styled dialogs, menus and controls built from interaction primitives.
guidance.caveat: Primitives are unstyled; supply styling, clear labels and test your assembled keyboard flow.

name: Base UI
description: Unstyled React components that supply interaction and accessibility behavior while you choose the appearance.

guidance.bestFor: Building a custom React design system with unstyled controls.
guidance.caveat: Compose and style the parts yourself; review portal stacking and backdrop setup.

name: React Aria
description: Adobe's customizable React components with keyboard interactions, accessibility and internationalization support.

guidance.bestFor: Add a due date field to a React assignment form so students can type a date or choose it from a calendar.
guidance.caveat: The date picker uses date objects from @internationalized/date. Parse saved date strings before passing them back to the field.

name: Headless UI
description: Unstyled interactive components for React and Vue that pair with your own CSS or Tailwind styles.

guidance.bestFor: Keyboard-friendly menus and accessible modal dialogs with your own visual design.
guidance.caveat: Your app controls when the dialog is open and supplies its title and styles. Use the examples for your framework.

name: Material UI
description: React components implementing Material Design, with examples for forms, navigation and application layouts.

guidance.bestFor: React dashboards, forms and application screens using Material Design components.
guidance.caveat: Default setup adds Emotion; check peer dependencies and framework integration before copying examples.

name: Mantine
description: A React component and hooks library for forms, overlays, data display and themed applications.

guidance.bestFor: React applications with ready-made controls, hooks and themes.
guidance.caveat: Follow your framework setup for styles and providers; optional packages require their own installation.

name: Chakra UI
description: Composable React components with accessible interactions and a styling system for consistent applications.

guidance.bestFor: Show whether a file upload is still running, has finished or has failed in a React app using a toast tied to the upload request.
guidance.caveat: Mount the Toaster in the app first. Connect the toast to the actual upload promise so it reports success only after the upload finishes.

name: Ant Design
description: A React UI system with application components for data-heavy screens, forms and navigation.

guidance.bestFor: Build a React homework dashboard that sorts assignments by due date and filters completed work out of a table.
guidance.caveat: Give each assignment a stable row key and supply its filter and sort rules. The table cannot infer what counts as completed from your data.

name: Fluent UI
description: Microsoft's design system with component guidance and implementation resources for product interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Add a confirmation dialog before a classmate discards unsaved notes in a React editor.
guidance.caveat: An alert dialog interrupts work and traps keyboard focus. Reserve it for choices with a cost, such as losing edits.

name: Carbon Design System
description: IBM's open-source design system with components, patterns and guidance for complex applications.

guidance.bestFor: Build a table for a lab inventory where students sort equipment and select several items for one action.
guidance.caveat: Keep long equipment histories on a details page. Carbon's expandable rows work best for short, supplementary details.

name: Primer
description: GitHub's design system with interface components, foundations and product design patterns.

guidance.bestFor: Put Rename, Duplicate and Archive in an actions menu beside each project in a React project list.
guidance.caveat: Give each action a descriptive label. If the current student cannot perform any actions, disable the menu trigger.

name: Adobe Spectrum
description: Adobe's design foundations, tokens and component resources for consistent cross-platform interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Decide where a form should show an error, such as an invalid email field or a homework file that failed to upload.
guidance.caveat: Toasts disappear. Keep an input error beside the field a student needs to fix, and reserve a toast for brief feedback about an action.

name: Bootstrap
description: A responsive interface toolkit with layout utilities, styled components and JavaScript interactions.

guidance.bestFor: Give a plain HTML club website a navigation bar that collapses into a menu on a phone.
guidance.caveat: The mobile menu toggle uses Bootstrap's Collapse JavaScript. Loading only the stylesheet leaves the toggle inactive.

name: Bulma
description: A CSS framework with responsive layouts and ready-made interface styles for HTML projects.

guidance.bestFor: Build a club website in HTML with navigation links across a laptop screen and a menu button on a phone.
guidance.caveat: Bulma supplies the styles. Wire up the menu button to toggle is-active on the button and menu, and update aria-expanded when it opens.

name: daisyUI
description: Tailwind CSS component classes and themes for building interfaces with concise HTML markup.

guidance.bestFor: Style a native HTML dialog in Tailwind so a student can preview a quiz question and return to editing it.
guidance.caveat: The dialog classes control its appearance. Wire the preview button to showModal() and provide a close control.

name: Flowbite
description: Tailwind CSS interface components and interactive patterns for building websites and applications.

guidance.bestFor: Add a dropdown for choosing a project action on a Tailwind site using HTML data attributes.
guidance.caveat: The dropdown needs Flowbite's JavaScript. If your app replaces its markup after loading, initialize the new dropdown after it renders.

name: Preline UI
description: Tailwind CSS components, blocks and templates with examples for marketing sites and applications.

guidance.bestFor: Build an FAQ for a class event where clicking a question reveals its answer.
guidance.caveat: Load Preline's accordion JavaScript and give each question and answer unique IDs so a copied button opens the right panel.

name: HyperUI
description: Copyable Tailwind CSS components for marketing pages, ecommerce screens and application interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Copy a styled contact form into a Tailwind site for a school club and adapt the fields to the information the club needs.
guidance.caveat: The examples use a placeholder form action. Connect a submission handler before promising visitors their message was sent.

name: Park UI
description: Styled components built with Ark UI and Panda CSS for creating a custom design system.

guidance.bestFor: Add a drag-and-drop file picker to a React assignment form and set how many attachments a student can select.
guidance.caveat: Set up Panda CSS and generate its styles before adding the component. The picker defaults to one file unless you change maxFiles.

name: Ark UI
description: Headless components for React, Vue, Solid and Svelte with shared interaction patterns.

guidance.bestFor: Build a custom-styled dialog that asks students to confirm deleting an assignment.
guidance.caveat: The dialog provides interaction behavior. Supply your own styles for the backdrop, panel and focus states.

name: HeroUI
description: Customizable React interface components combining Tailwind styling with accessible interaction behavior.

guidance.bestFor: Open a React signup form in a modal with a scrollable body and a visible close button.
guidance.caveat: Import HeroUI’s styles and choose where long forms should scroll so the close button stays reachable.

name: Aceternity UI
description: React and Tailwind components for animated landing pages, backgrounds and distinctive visual effects.

guidance.bestFor: Give a portfolio project card a layered 3D tilt as the pointer moves over it.
guidance.caveat: The depth effect depends on hover. Keep the title and project link visible on touchscreens.

name: Magic UI
description: Animated React components and effects for landing pages, product demos and marketing interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Create a scrolling row of club logos across a React landing page.
guidance.caveat: Pausing on hover is optional and only helps pointer users. Provide a way to pause or read a stationary row.

name: React Bits
description: Preview animated text, backgrounds and interactive cards. Copy the React source for the individual effect you want.

guidance.bestFor: Build an animated portfolio heading using the SplitText component in an existing React app.
guidance.caveat: Pick the JavaScript or TypeScript version that matches the app and choose either plain CSS or Tailwind before copying.

name: Motion Primitives
description: Customizable animated interface components for building transitions and interactions in React.

guidance.bestFor: Animate a scoreboard total from its previous number to its new value in React.
guidance.caveat: The spring animates a number you supply. Keep the actual score in application state so it remains accurate during animation.

name: Tremor
description: Copy React and Tailwind components for dashboard charts, date filters and metric cards. The component source is open and the premium blocks are separate.

guidance.bestFor: Compare survey responses across classes in a dashboard bar chart.
guidance.caveat: Tremor’s copyable chart requires Tailwind CSS 4 or later. The chart’s index and category names must match keys in your data.

name: Web Awesome
description: Framework-independent web components for forms, navigation and application UI.

guidance.bestFor: Add a settings dialog to an HTML project using the wa-dialog custom element.
guidance.caveat: Give the dialog an accessible label even when you hide its header.

name: PatternFly
description: Application components and design guidance for tables, dashboards, navigation and enterprise workflows.

guidance.bestFor: Build an admin table where staff can sort rows and expand one record to inspect its details.
guidance.caveat: For sortable columns, track the current sort direction and update the displayed row order when a header is activated.

name: PrimeReact
description: A React UI suite with configurable components for forms, data display and application layouts.

guidance.bestFor: Build a searchable equipment inventory with paginated rows and filters for individual columns.
guidance.caveat: In the unstyled DataTable, you compose the filters, sorting controls and table markup yourself. Pick a styled version if you want the library to supply the visual treatment.

name: PrimeVue
description: A Vue UI suite with configurable components for forms, tables and application interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Add a keyboard-accessible modal to a Vue project, such as a confirmation dialog before deleting an assignment.
guidance.caveat: Enable modal behavior to keep keyboard focus inside. Your trigger button must report which dialog it controls and whether it is open.

name: Vuetify
description: A Vue component framework with Material Design styles and responsive application building blocks.

guidance.bestFor: Show a large assignment archive in a Vue table that fetches one page at a time.
guidance.caveat: The server-side table reports page, sort and search changes. Your API must apply them before returning the rows.

name: Naive UI
description: A TypeScript-based Vue component library with configurable themes and application controls.

guidance.bestFor: Build a paginated Vue sign-up roster where a teacher can select several students at once.
guidance.caveat: Give each row a stable unique key so selections still identify the same student after a page change.

name: Element Plus
description: Vue interface components and design guidance for building desktop-oriented web applications.

guidance.bestFor: Build a Vue event registration form that validates each field and can reset an unfinished entry.
guidance.caveat: For validation and reset to work, each form item’s prop must point to the matching key in the form model.

name: Quasar
description: A Vue framework with interface components and tooling for web, mobile and desktop applications.

guidance.bestFor: Display a club inventory as a searchable table on laptops and as cards on small screens.
guidance.caveat: Set a unique row key before enabling selection. If you paginate on the server, supply the total row count as well.

name: Skeleton
description: A design system with Tailwind utilities, themes and interactive interface components.

guidance.bestFor: Make a themed FAQ accordion where students can keep two answers open for comparison.
guidance.caveat: The accordion opens one item at a time by default. Enable multiple expansion when readers need to compare answers.

name: Bits UI
description: Headless Svelte components for building custom controls with accessible interaction behavior.

guidance.bestFor: Build a Svelte course picker where typing narrows the list and the keyboard selects a course.
guidance.caveat: Wire the typed query to your own filtered list so users see the matching courses.

name: Melt UI
description: Build unstyled Svelte controls such as dialogs, tabs and toggles. The Svelte 5 edition uses the melt package and has its own installation guide.

guidance.bestFor: Build a Svelte autocomplete picker with custom markup for a student directory.
guidance.caveat: The combobox builder supplies the behaviors and state. You attach them to the input and list and supply the styling.

name: Lucide
description: Consistent line icons with adjustable size, color and stroke width for web interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Consistent interface icons with adjustable size, color and stroke.
guidance.caveat: Import only the icons you use and provide text labels for icon-only actions.

name: Heroicons
description: SVG interface icons from Tailwind's creators, available in outline and solid styles.

guidance.bestFor: Give a React or Vue toolbar clear icons for search, editing and navigation, with smaller glyphs for dense controls.
guidance.caveat: Use the import path for the intended size. The 16px and 20px sets are solid, while the 24px set also offers outlines.

name: Tabler Icons
description: A searchable collection of vector icons for apps, websites and design systems.

guidance.bestFor: Match a settings sidebar and a compact data table with the same SVG icons, adjusting stroke width to stay legible at each size.
guidance.caveat: Import individual icons by name so the bundler can leave out the rest of the set.

name: Phosphor Icons
description: A flexible icon family with multiple weights for interfaces, diagrams and presentations.

guidance.bestFor: Use an outlined heart for an unsaved item and the same heart in a filled weight after a student saves it.
guidance.caveat: Expose the saved state in the button's accessible name or pressed state so the change in icon weight is also available to screen reader users.

name: Iconify
description: Search and use icons from many icon sets through shared tools and framework integrations.

guidance.bestFor: Build a searchable icon picker that uses names from several icon collections in the same interface.
guidance.caveat: On-demand icons need network access the first time they load. Bundle the icons for essential controls if the app must work offline.

name: Simple Icons
description: SVG brand icons for identifying services, developer tools and supported integrations.

guidance.bestFor: Show recognizable GitHub, Figma and other brand marks beside the tools a student lists in a project portfolio.
guidance.caveat: Check each brand's usage rules before recoloring a logo. Some records have no guidelines link, so follow up with the brand itself.

name: Remix Icon
description: A neutral-style icon system with outlined and filled symbols for application interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Give a mobile tab bar matching outline and filled symbols for its inactive and selected tabs.
guidance.caveat: When using the icon font, load its stylesheet and use the exact line or fill class name. A missing stylesheet can leave a control blank.

name: Material Symbols
description: Google's configurable interface symbols, available as icon fonts and individual SVG assets.

guidance.bestFor: Switch the same bookmark symbol from outlined to filled when an article is saved, keeping its alignment steady.
guidance.caveat: For a web font, request only your icon names and the axes you actually vary. The full font includes thousands of unused symbols.

name: Matter.js
description: A browser physics engine for 2D bodies, collisions, gravity, constraints and interactive simulations.

guidance.bestFor: Interactive 2D bodies, collisions and physics experiments.
guidance.caveat: You must integrate rendering and lifecycle cleanup and provide alternatives to pointer-only interaction.

name: Motion
description: Animation tools for React and JavaScript, including gestures, layout transitions and scroll effects.

guidance.bestFor: React entrance, exit, layout and gesture animations.
guidance.caveat: Plan reduced-motion behavior and keyboard equivalents for gesture interactions.

name: GSAP
description: JavaScript animation tools for sequencing motion, controlling timelines and building scroll-driven effects.

guidance.bestFor: Coordinate a title, illustration and caption so a student can pause or replay the whole introduction with one control.
guidance.caveat: Put the steps on one timeline and position them there. Separate delays have to be recalculated when an earlier step changes length.

name: React Spring
description: Spring-based animation primitives for fluid React interface movement and interactive transitions.

guidance.bestFor: Make a React drawer slide into place with a spring and respond if the user closes it before the opening motion finishes.
guidance.caveat: Pass animated values to an animated element and choose the web package for a DOM project. Tune the spring with the actual drawer distance.

name: AutoAnimate
description: Automatically animates elements entering, leaving or moving within a container across JavaScript frameworks.

guidance.bestFor: Animate an assignment list when adding work, deleting a row or reordering items by due date.
guidance.caveat: Attach it to the parent whose direct children move. Updating text inside an existing child does not trigger a list animation.

name: Three.js
description: A JavaScript 3D library with examples for scenes, materials, lighting and interactive visual experiences.

guidance.bestFor: Interactive 3D scenes and graphics in the browser.
guidance.caveat: Scene setup, rendering, asset loading and performance need deliberate work; keep essential content accessible outside the canvas.

name: Anime.js
description: A JavaScript animation engine for coordinated DOM, CSS and SVG motion.

guidance.bestFor: Sequence a set of shapes in an interactive diagram so an arrow and its caption can move at different points on the same timeline.
guidance.caveat: The current timeline examples import createTimeline. Check the installed Anime.js version before using an older snippet.

name: Codrops
description: Read frontend case studies and follow interaction tutorials with runnable demos for typography, transitions and creative coding.

guidance.bestFor: Follow a worked visual tutorial to build one effect, such as a scroll-driven image reveal in a portfolio.
guidance.caveat: Check the individual tutorial's stack first. For example, the Astro landing-page tutorial uses GSAP and canvas, while other demos depend on React or Three.js.

name: Siteinspire
description: Filter real websites by style, layout, sector or platform, then follow a reference to its designer or agency.

guidance.bestFor: Find typographic or grid-based portfolios and choose a layout direction for a student photography site.
guidance.caveat: Give your agent the particular site you selected and name the layout decision. A gallery thumbnail leaves mobile and keyboard behavior unspecified.

name: Landbook
description: Browse examples of how real sites handle landing pages, type and editorial layout. The full gallery requires a subscription.

guidance.bestFor: Compare how landing pages and storefronts introduce the product before sketching the first screen of your own site.
guidance.caveat: Open the underlying site to inspect how the layout responds at different widths. A saved screenshot captures a single view.

name: Lapa Ninja
description: Landing-page examples grouped by industry, visual style and page type.

guidance.bestFor: Study the sequence of sections in a full-page landing screenshot before writing a product page for your own app.
guidance.caveat: Check the capture date or visit the original. The gallery includes past versions, so your reference may differ from the live website.

name: One Page Love
description: One-page website examples and templates for portfolios, product launches and focused landing pages.

guidance.bestFor: Compare separate hero and signup section examples to plan a single-page launch website for a class project.
guidance.caveat: Record whether you chose a showcased website, a section example or a downloadable template before asking your agent to use it.

name: Mobbin
description: Study real onboarding, navigation and checkout screens across apps and websites. Full library access and the agent connector require a paid plan.

guidance.bestFor: Map the steps of a mobile onboarding flow by comparing screens from shipped apps before designing your own first-run experience.
guidance.caveat: Write down the action that moves between screens and test it in your prototype. Screenshots alone cannot demonstrate validation or focus behavior.

name: Curated Design
description: Website design references categorized by industry and style for exploring a project's visual direction.

guidance.bestFor: Find websites by industry and style to compare typography and hierarchy for a portfolio or product homepage.
guidance.caveat: Open the referenced site and point your agent to a particular page or section. The gallery preview alone gives little information about its responsive layout.

name: Hoverstat.es
description: An archive of experimental web design and unusual interactions for creative interface research.

guidance.bestFor: Find an example of a reactive menu, cursor treatment or image hover effect to prototype in a portfolio.
guidance.caveat: For a pointer-driven example, design a tap or keyboard equivalent before building it into navigation.

name: Agent Skills
description: The Agent Skills format specification and guidance for packaging reusable instructions and resources for agents.

guidance.bestFor: Turn a repeated task, such as reviewing a teammate's pull request, into a SKILL.md that a compatible agent can reuse.
guidance.caveat: The skill name must match its folder. Describe when it should run so an agent can pick it for the right task.

name: Anthropic Skills
description: Anthropic's published skill examples for studying reusable agent workflows and task-specific instructions.

guidance.bestFor: Use the webapp-testing example to help Claude open a local app, try a broken interaction and capture what the browser shows.
guidance.caveat: That example runs Python Playwright scripts. A classmate needs a working Python and browser setup to repeat your check.

name: Vercel Agent Skills
description: Vercel's agent skill collection covering frontend practices, interface review and related development workflows.

guidance.bestFor: Ask an agent why a React dashboard loads slowly. Its React performance skill covers requests that wait on each other and code shipped to the browser.
guidance.caveat: Some rules use Next.js server features. On a plain React site, start with the client rules and measure the page before and after a change.

name: GitHub Spec Kit
description: Templates and workflows for turning a product idea into explicit requirements and an implementation plan.

guidance.bestFor: Turn a team's idea for a shared assignment tracker into a written feature spec, a plan and tasks that teammates can review.
guidance.caveat: The quick start needs Python 3.11 or newer and uv. Budget time to review the spec and plan before the agent starts building.

name: AGENTS.md
description: A documented format for giving coding agents project context, commands and working conventions.

guidance.bestFor: Give every teammate's coding agent the same instructions for starting the app, running tests and working in the team's project folders.
guidance.caveat: A closer AGENTS.md can override the root file. Put commands that apply only to one project in that project's folder.

name: Superpowers
description: An agent skill framework with workflows for brainstorming, planning, debugging and verifying software changes.

guidance.bestFor: Have an agent break a multiplayer feature into small changes, write a failing test for each one and review the work as it goes.
guidance.caveat: The full workflow adds a design review and a written plan. Set aside time to read them before approving implementation.

name: Claude Code Best Practices
description: Official guidance for giving an agent useful context, structuring tasks and verifying its work.

guidance.bestFor: Give Claude Code a bug it can reproduce, such as a filter that hides unfinished work, and ask for a test that proves the fix.
guidance.caveat: Choose what counts as proof. A passing test can check the filter logic, but a layout change may need a browser screenshot.

name: ARIA Authoring Practices
description: W3C patterns and examples for implementing accessible widgets, keyboard interactions and interface semantics.

guidance.bestFor: Planning keyboard behavior and semantics for custom widgets.
guidance.caveat: Examples are guidance, not a certification of your app; test the implemented widget with keyboards and assistive technology.

name: MDN Learn
description: Structured web-development lessons covering HTML, CSS, JavaScript and the foundations behind browser applications.

guidance.bestFor: Build a signup form with native HTML inputs or open a modal with the browser's dialog element.
guidance.caveat: Start with the forms lesson. Storing the submitted answers still requires a destination in your app.

name: web.dev Learn
description: Google's web courses on CSS, accessibility, performance, responsive design and browser fundamentals.

guidance.bestFor: Improve a form that is hard to fill out on a phone. Work through autofill, validation and testing.
guidance.caveat: The lessons teach browser behavior. Test your actual form with the keyboard and the input types you chose.

name: Learn React
description: The official React tutorial with interactive examples for components, state and sharing data.

guidance.bestFor: Learning components, props, state, events and shared data with examples.
guidance.caveat: Reading examples needs little setup; building your own app still requires a project environment and JavaScript foundations.

name: TypeScript Handbook
description: TypeScript's official guide to types, narrowing, functions and the language's core concepts.

guidance.bestFor: Fix a TypeScript error when a search result might be a string, an object or null.
guidance.caveat: Checking a type in your code helps narrow a union. A type annotation alone cannot validate an incoming API response.

name: JavaScript.info
description: Learn JavaScript through short lessons and exercises, from writing a constructor for a calculator to handling browser events and asynchronous code.

guidance.bestFor: Trace what happens between clicking a button and its event handler running.
guidance.caveat: The examples attach handlers to DOM elements. In a framework, use its event conventions for the same behavior.

name: The Odin Project
description: A project-based web-development curriculum that combines lessons with applications you build yourself.

guidance.bestFor: Build a landing page or calculator while practicing Git, CSS layout and DOM events.
guidance.caveat: The Foundations projects assume you work in a local editor. Allow time for Git and command-line setup.

name: freeCodeCamp
description: A coding curriculum with exercises and projects across web development and computer science.

guidance.bestFor: Find a small coding exercise to practice the skill your agent just used before changing your own project.
guidance.caveat: An exercise checks its own requirements. Repeat the change in your project to see whether you can apply it there.

name: Full Stack Open
description: A university course on building modern web applications with React, Node.js, APIs and databases.

guidance.bestFor: Connect a React interface to a Node.js API and follow the request through both parts of the app.
guidance.caveat: The course assumes programming experience and basic familiarity with web development, databases and Git.

name: CS50x
description: Harvard's introductory computer science course with lectures, problem sets and a final project.

guidance.bestFor: Practice explaining why an algorithm works before asking an agent to optimize it.
guidance.caveat: Choose the lecture or problem set that matches your question. Early algorithm examples use C, so translate the idea to your app's language.

name: The Coding Train Physics
description: Follow Matter.js video experiments with bodies, collisions, constraints and dragging. The lesson notes flag older Engine.run examples.

guidance.bestFor: Build a Plinko board or a draggable pendulum and see how bodies and constraints affect the motion.
guidance.caveat: Some videos show older engine calls. Check the project's installed Matter.js version before copying the setup.

name: Master.dev Front-End Bootcamp
description: Video lessons on HTML, CSS and JavaScript lead to a calculator and a browser game. The free course requires an account.

guidance.bestFor: Use the calculator project to practice turning a design into HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
guidance.caveat: This is a sequence of classes and exercises. Pick the relevant lesson if you already have a working project.

name: Interactive Flexbox Guide
description: Josh Comeau's interactive explanation of alignment, sizing, wrapping and space distribution in CSS Flexbox.

guidance.bestFor: Find out why a toolbar overflows on a narrow screen by changing item size, shrink and wrap in a live example.
guidance.caveat: The demo isolates flex layout. Reproduce the problem with the same parent width and text lengths as your page.

name: Storybook
description: Build, document and test interface components separately from the rest of an application.

guidance.bestFor: See a component's empty, loading and populated states side by side without walking through the whole app.
guidance.caveat: You supply each story's props and context. A story with mock data still needs a separate check against the real service.

name: Playwright
description: Browser automation and end-to-end testing for checking real user workflows across browser engines.

guidance.bestFor: Checking complete user journeys in real browser engines.
guidance.caveat: Browser binaries and a running app are needed; assertions still depend on the scenarios you write.

name: Vitest
description: A JavaScript and TypeScript testing framework for fast unit tests and component checks.

guidance.bestFor: Fast unit tests for JavaScript and TypeScript logic.
guidance.caveat: Check the current Node and Vite requirements; DOM and real-browser tests need additional environment setup.

name: Testing Library
description: Interface-testing utilities that locate and exercise elements in ways that resemble user behavior.

guidance.bestFor: Test a login form by finding its labeled inputs and submit button, then checking the message a student sees after submitting.
guidance.caveat: These helpers need a test runner and a browser or simulated DOM. Use a real browser to check whether the form fits on a phone.

name: axe-core
description: An accessibility testing engine for detecting supported categories of issues in web interfaces.

guidance.bestFor: Check a website for accessibility issues by scanning the login form and its error state during a browser test.
guidance.caveat: The scan can flag issues for manual review and covers only some accessibility requirements. Try the form with a keyboard as well.

name: Chrome DevTools
description: Browser tools and guides for inspecting layouts, debugging JavaScript and measuring page performance.

guidance.bestFor: Debug an image or API request that never appears by checking its URL, status and response headers.
guidance.caveat: The Network panel records while it is open. Reload or repeat the action before inspecting a missing request.

name: CodePen
description: An online coding environment for experimenting with interfaces and sharing runnable web examples.

guidance.bestFor: Share a small reproduction of a broken button, animation or CSS layout with a live preview.
guidance.caveat: Match the dependencies and preprocessing used in your real app. A Pen can run with different settings.

name: Excalidraw
description: A hand-drawn-style whiteboard for sketching interface ideas, system diagrams and user flows.

guidance.bestFor: Sketch the screens and decisions in a sign-in flow and give the diagram to your coding agent.
guidance.caveat: An exported image communicates the flow. Keep the editable drawing if you want to rearrange its elements later.

name: Penpot
description: An open-source design platform for interface mockups, reusable components and developer handoff.

guidance.bestFor: Test how a user moves from a project list to a detail screen by connecting boards in a clickable prototype.
guidance.caveat: Prototype links simulate navigation. The agent still needs to implement routing and decide where data comes from.

name: Designeer
description: A gallery of interface and motion experiments with creator credits, clips and extracted color palettes.

guidance.bestFor: Pick a short interaction, follow it to its creator and describe the specific behavior you want to build.
guidance.caveat: Clips show the result. Follow the creator link for implementation details and reuse terms.

name: Detail
description: Small product design decisions explained through real examples, including keyboard hints, interface copy and accessible controls.

guidance.bestFor: Give an agent one interaction to reproduce, such as revealing a shortcut beside the control it operates.
guidance.caveat: Some entries show a video or a product observation. Use an example as a behavior spec and test your own implementation.

name: Motionimo Frames
description: Browse individual motion-design frames by color, mood, style and composition, then follow the creator credit.

guidance.bestFor: Find a still that demonstrates the lighting or composition you want, then compare similar frames.
guidance.caveat: A still establishes a visual direction. It does not tell your agent the animation timing or grant permission to reuse the image.

name: Amicro
description: React microinteractions with live previews and source, including a search button that swaps its icon on hover.

guidance.bestFor: Choose a single state change, inspect its preview, then give your agent that specific component and its setup.
guidance.caveat: Check each example's imports, icon dependency and attribution. Test the interaction with a keyboard as well as a pointer.

name: Paaages
description: Full-page website references grouped by screen type, including sign-in, pricing, landing and 404 pages.

guidance.bestFor: Compare layouts for the exact screen your project needs before asking an agent to build it.
guidance.caveat: Screenshots capture one state. Visit the original site to check responsive behavior and interactions.

name: Gradientora
description: Explore ready-made gradients or open the shader playground to change an orb’s lighting, surface noise and motion.

guidance.bestFor: Use the sphere editor to compare a rim highlight, surface noise and a slower animation before designing your own orb.
guidance.caveat: Many downloadable gradient packs are premium. The editor can serve as a visual reference with no asset download.

name: Introducing Geist Serif
description: Vercel's type specimen and design notes on pairing serif display titles with Geist Sans controls and body text.

guidance.bestFor: Compare the same resource title in serif and sans, then use the specimen to judge size, contrast and hierarchy.
guidance.caveat: Use the official font distribution and keep its license when self-hosting the files.

name: DesignBookmark
description: A directory of design tools grouped by task, including typography, gradients, design systems and 3D motion.

guidance.bestFor: Find a tool for a specific design job, such as checking a palette's contrast, and follow the listing to the original tool.
guidance.caveat: Some listings are sponsored. Check the linked tool for current access and pricing.

name: Insposite
description: A screenshot gallery with distinct filters for portfolios, inspiration sites and working design tools.

guidance.bestFor: Compare a portfolio to another portfolio, or switch to Tools to discover resources you can use in a build.
guidance.caveat: Gallery cards can lead to third-party products with different terms. Follow the original destination before choosing one.

name: Kinetics
description: Preview interface animations and tune a spring's stiffness, damping and mass before copying a CSS or React example.

guidance.bestFor: Tune overshoot for a button or panel with the generator and hand the matching code to your agent.
guidance.caveat: CSS, React and prompt availability vary by example. Spring parameters here describe UI motion, not collisions in a Matter.js world.

name: The Component Gallery
description: Compare how different design systems implement the same component, with filters for framework, accessibility notes and examples.

guidance.bestFor: Look up a popover or button and compare markup, usage and accessibility guidance before choosing an implementation.
guidance.caveat: Examples belong to different systems. Follow the example's own docs for API compatibility and license terms.

name: mapcn
description: React map components for adding markers, popups and controls to a MapLibre map styled with Tailwind.

guidance.bestFor: Build a campus map with a custom marker and a popup before layering in your own locations.
guidance.caveat: Check the tile provider's terms and attribution when changing the basemap or publishing a project.

name: Craft by Gustavo Fior
description: Short interaction design lessons with live examples of button presses, interruption and when a hover effect helps.

guidance.bestFor: Compare how a button feels across press states, then give the agent a precise description of the one you want.
guidance.caveat: Start with a published lesson such as Button Press. Some topics in the index are still planned.

name: UI Skills
description: A directory of named skills for coding agents, including guides for improving interface motion and accessibility.

guidance.bestFor: Look up an individual skill and read its instructions before deciding whether it suits the project.
guidance.caveat: Skill authors and requirements vary. Follow the original source and inspect the instructions before running an installer.

name: Graphical
description: A visual theme builder that turns design choices into a GUI.md file and React components for a coding agent.

guidance.bestFor: Translate a chosen type scale and theme into a specification an agent can follow consistently across screens.
guidance.caveat: The complete builder and exports are paid. Explore the public preview before choosing it for a class project.

name: Canvas UI
description: Experimental shader effects for interface components, with live examples, framework-specific setup and plain HTML fallbacks.

guidance.bestFor: Prototype an optional material effect on a single control and compare it with the ordinary HTML fallback.
guidance.caveat: Many effects depend on experimental HTML-in-canvas support. Verify the fallback and test on the actual classroom browser.

name: Transitions.dev
description: A collection of interface transition recipes with copyable examples and a companion motion skill for agents.

guidance.bestFor: Choose a transition for a real UI state change and use the companion skill to describe the timing to an agent.
guidance.caveat: The core collection is free and some additional recipes are paid. Check the specific transition before adopting it.

name: Paper Shaders
description: Interactive shader examples with adjustable parameters, including a smoke ring with controls for its radius, thickness, noise and speed.

guidance.bestFor: Tune a luminous ring in the browser and compare a moving state with a static frame before using the effect in a project.
guidance.caveat: Continuous shader animation uses rendering time. Try speed zero for reduced motion and test on the intended device.
